page: Amazon Web Services c5a.large is a compute-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7R32 processor running at 3.3 GHz. The instance provides 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads per core, utilizing a dedicated CPU allocation. It is equipped with 4.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, translating to 2.0 GB of RAM per core. There is no bundled local storage or GPU acceleration, and the baseline network bandwidth is rated at 1 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate that the c5a.large delivers modest performance relative to the broader cloud market. Single-core and multi-core stress-ng tests score at 767.58, placing the instance in the bottom 10% of tested hardware. Similarly, Geekbench multi-core (1593.0), compiling (1837.0), and ray tracing (1986.0) benchmarks fall into the bottom 10%. However, single-threaded operations show moderate capability, with Geekbench single-core scoring 1263.0 and gzip compression reaching 23.95 GB/sec, both ranking in the middle 50%. Memory bandwidth is a notable bottleneck, with uncached read and write speeds of 24.05 GB/sec and 20.03 GB/sec respectively, which are categorized as weak.

Given its dedicated CPU allocation and 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the c5a.large offers a predictable but entry-level compute profile. It lacks local NVMe storage and high-speed networking, which limits its utility for data-intensive or high-throughput database operations, as reflected in its low Passmark database score of 732.47 and Redis SET throughput of 1.83 million operations per second. This instance is best suited for lightweight, compute-focused workloads that require dedicated CPU resources but do not demand high memory capacity or rapid storage I/O, such as basic single-threaded processing, small-scale web serving, or minor utility scripting.
